- **The tool registry's builtin SET is ctor-frozen.** `refreshRuntimeConfig` / preset hot-reload re-resolves the system prompt and next-turn behavior, but a config change that *adds or removes a builtin tool* only takes effect on session restart. `applyBuiltinOverrideVisibility` can hide an already-registered tool per-turn; it cannot re-add one the constructor omitted.
**One-line role.** Built-in agent presets that bundle a default prompt, a built-in-tool whitelist, and safe permission shortcuts so the engine can stay domain-agnostic.
// joins the preset's section .md files into one system prompt
function buildPresetSystemPrompt(preset: AgentPreset): string;
**Prompt composition** (`prompt/composer.ts`) — the resolved preset drives both git-status injection and the behavior sections:
return buildPresetSystemPrompt(preset);

This module defines the contract an external repo implements to turn CodeShell into a concrete agent application, and the single `defineProduct()` call that materializes it. The three-layer model is: **Preset** (system prompt + tool set + permission defaults), **Adapter** (custom tools, MCP servers, tool enable/disable, extra permission rules, hooks), and **Contract** (evaluators, default tags/metadata, turn/token limits, concurrency). `defineProduct()` registers the preset, builds an evaluator, collects custom tools, and wires a fully configured `RunManager`. It does not run the agent itself — the caller drives the returned `manager` via `submit`/`resume`/`cancel`.

- **`customPrompt` beats `sections`.** If both are set, the full custom prompt wins; `sections` is ignored. When neither preset `sections` nor `customPrompt` is given, sections default to `["base", "orchestration"]`.

record.title: Ambiguous system prompt precedence not enforced
record.detail: Lines 158-159 pass both customSystemPrompt (from presetDef.customPrompt) and appendSystemPrompt to RunManager. The ProductPreset interface allows both customPrompt and sections to be defined. The comment at lines 38-41 of types.ts documents that customPrompt should take precedence, but this function does not validate or enforce that — it could pass both sections and customPrompt to RunManager, causing ambiguity about which takes effect.
record.fix: Add validation: if presetDef.customPrompt is defined, do not build agentPreset.promptSections (set to empty array or undefined). Only pass one system prompt approach to RunManager.

record.title: System prompt uses UTC date instead of local date
record.detail: Line 64 uses `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` which returns the UTC date, not the local date. For a user in UTC+8 on 2026-05-30 at 23:00, this returns 2026-05-29 (the next UTC day), not the local 2026-05-30. The system prompt should reflect the user's local date.
record.fix: Use `new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA')` instead of `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` to get the local date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

record.title: Ambiguous system prompt precedence not enforced
record.detail: Lines 158-159 pass both customSystemPrompt (from presetDef.customPrompt) and appendSystemPrompt to RunManager. The ProductPreset interface allows both customPrompt and sections to be defined. The comment at lines 38-41 of types.ts documents that customPrompt should take precedence, but this function does not validate or enforce that — it could pass both sections and customPrompt to RunManager, causing ambiguity about which takes effect.
record.fix: Add validation: if presetDef.customPrompt is defined, do not build agentPreset.promptSections (set to empty array or undefined). Only pass one system prompt approach to RunManager.
record.verify_note: This is a real contract violation: the documented behavior (customPrompt takes precedence) is not implemented. Both the custom system prompt and the default sections appear in the final system prompt, which may confuse users who expect customPrompt to replace the default behavior entirely. However, this doesn't cause crashes or incorrect tool execution — it only results in both prompt contents being present, which is suboptimal but not catastrophic. The fix suggested by the reviewer (check if customPrompt is defined and exclude promptSections) is sound and straightforward.
record.verify_reason: The code at define.ts lines 158-159 passes both customSystemPrompt and promptSections to RunManager/Engine. In composer.ts, the PromptComposer unconditionally includes both a "custom_system" section (if customSystemPrompt exists, lines 141-146) and a "behavior" section (always, lines 166-172) that loads the promptSections. According to types.ts lines 38-41, customPrompt should "take precedence" over sections, but the implementation doesn't enforce this — both are included in the final system prompt. Additionally, define.ts line 113 sets promptSections to default ["base", "orchestration"] even when customPrompt is defined, as long as sections isn't explicitly set to undefined.

record.title: System prompt uses UTC date instead of local date
record.detail: Line 64 uses `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` which returns the UTC date, not the local date. For a user in UTC+8 on 2026-05-30 at 23:00, this returns 2026-05-29 (the next UTC day), not the local 2026-05-30. The system prompt should reflect the user's local date.
record.fix: Use `new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA')` instead of `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` to get the local date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
record.verify_note: This is a real but low-impact defect. The date mismatch only occurs for users east of UTC (roughly 1/3 of the world) and only during the early-to-mid part of their day when UTC is still showing the previous date. While it does provide incorrect context to the LLM, it's an informational field rather than a functional failure. The impact is that the LLM receives an incorrect "today" date in system-reminder messages, which could affect date-based reasoning.
record.verify_reason: Line 64 uses `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` which returns the UTC date, not the local date. For users in timezones ahead of UTC (UTC+1 through UTC+12), during their local morning/noon hours, the UTC date will be the previous calendar day. For example, a user in UTC+8 on May 31 at 10:00 AM local time would see "Today's date is 2026-05-30" because UTC shows 2026-05-30 02:00. The date is used in the system-reminder message prepended to all user context, so it directly affects what date the LLM sees as "today". The proposed fix using `toLocaleDateString('en-CA')` correctly addresses this by using the client's local timezone.
